meta_description_en: Reviews of the molecular modeling software MOLGRUM by Dr. Ian Hughes and the disk management utility DISC ORGANISER for Disciple/+D systems.
meta_description_ru: Обзоры программы для молекулярного моделирования MOLGRUM от д-ра Яна Хьюза и утилиты для работы с дисками DISC ORGANISER для систем Disciple/+D.
body_en_plain:
Product        Reviewed by  Page
-------        -----------  ----


MOLGRUM        Brian Cavers  02


DISC ORGANISER C.Grant Dixon 13

    MOLGRUM by Dr. Ian Hughes
    -reviewed by Brian Cavers
    -------------------------


MOLGRUM enables the construction
and display of three-dimensional
"stick and ball" representations
of molecules which can be SAVEd,
re-LOADed,edited,printed,zoomed,
rotated, scrolled and animated.
Though written for a specialized
field, MOLGRUM can portray not
only molecules but other shapes
in 3D and should interest anyone
who likes wireframe graphics.

MOLGRUM is supplied with a demo
graphic to let the user become
more familiar with the software.

Main control is by user-defined,
UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT/SELECT keys
which move a BRIGHT panel left
and right over menu bars at the
foot of the screen.There are 5
main menus accessed by selecting
UP/DOWN and some choices branch
to sub menus. Although stated in
the instructions I felt it might
be worth emphasising the UP/DOWN
link again and also strengthen
the indicator on each main menu
by changing it from an upright
arrow to perhaps an up and down
arrow UDG? I also thought routes
to sub menus should be shown in
the manual too as I often found

options listed therein to which
I could find no route. For
example, on the page for menu 21
it COULD say, [reach here from
option d on menu 4 via menu 23]
It took me 15 minutes to find
that information!Apart from that
the manual is excellent - well
produced to a high standard with
masses of detailed information
on using and modifying MOLGRUM.

I know little about molecules so
decided to try to construct a
cube to test the software's ease
of use.

Selecting EDIT I found a section
in which I INPUT the coordinates
of the corners of my imaginary
cube. I entered...

50,50,0 then...  50,100,0...
100,100,0;   and 100,50,0 - the
first two of each group being
the x,y position on the screen
and the zero being the z
coordinate or "depth".That would
represent a flat square. I then
entered the same values but
replaced the zero with 50 to be
an identical square 50 pixels
"above" (or behind!) the first
square - thus forming a cube.

Two other values had to be INPUT
- the name of the atom(when used
for its true purpose (each
coordinate is the position of an
atom in the molecule) and its
RESIDUE number. I entered C(from
the manual) for the atom and 5
for the residue (a wild guess as

I had no idea what this was but
entering 5 did no harm!).

Input is excellent-you can enter
in sequence and correct/modify
by cursoring up down and across
a table of values.You can return
later at any time-very flexible!

I then went to the animation
menu to see the result and found
I had created 8 dots which could
be moved in obvious relationship
like a cubic star cluster!

Back to the manual and I found
an option to JOIN which involved
placing a cross-hair cursor over
any two successive points and
pressing SELECT. Pretty soon I
had my wire-frame cube!

From the animation menu I could
twist it, turn it, zoom in and
out,move it round the screen and
finally- take a snapshot of each
move and run them in sequence.
The data for the structure can
be SAVEd or the whole"film show"
as well as any individual screen
as a SCREEN$.

I SAVEd two successive frames as
SCREEN$ and have included them
here to give you a slight idea
of the images and the sense of
movement.

Keep pressing the GRAPHICS key
(SHIFT+9 if you have no GRAPHICS
key) to switch between the two
frames.Any other key returns you
here...

If you press GRAPHICS again on
this page you can see one frame
from the demo molecule to show
you the sort of thing a chemist
might be interested in creating
and examining. Actually,this one
frame does not do justice to the
data that is behind it.Remember,
these images can be rotated in
any direction or zoomed up close
without losing resolution like
most art programs.

MOLGRUM has three COPY options.
One uses the BASIC keyword COPY
if your printer interface can
handle it or I suppose a ZX-type
printer would work.The other two
are machine code routines - one
being large-sized (again without
losing resolution).

At first I thought there seemed
to be a bug here.On both my Opus
Centronics and Interface 1 I got
a column of the letter K down
the left-hand margin.However,the
loader program has the printer
codes stored as BASIC DATA and I
soon found that by replacing the
codes in line 58 and 66 with 0's
the problem was cured. That is
the advantage of having an"open"
program that can be customised!
As supplied, MOLGRUM is set up
for the Epson LX80 printer which
presumably needs the codes in
lines 58 and 66.


The program comes on tape or
Opus disk but is not too hard to
customise for other systems.

There is an option to alter the
file-size and by reducing this I
made room for the extra space
demanded by Interface 1. The
program is very open and Ian has
supplied a wealth of info to
help you customize it - even to
programming details. The printer
codes listing is another example
of this helpfulness and even REM
comments can be MERGEd!

Capital letters are POKEd ON at
the start of the program but I
don't think they are after using
INPUT.  I entered a filename in
lower case and later found I
could not escape an animation
sequence until I used CAPS SHIFT
(although other controls seemed
normal).

There are very many other little
details in MOLGRUM which give it
great flexibility, such as...

Printing out data in table form.

Molecular information (which was
beyond my understanding).

Altering step rates.

Rotation about either the centre
or about one coordinate.

Representation of the atoms as
spheres (with different shade
patterns)or diamonds or squares!

Varying size of same or simply
show as points; redefine pattern
shading and so on and on and on!

Although I have spent many hours
with this program over several
sessions, I cannot do it justice
in the time I have available but
I've seen enough to say MOLGRUM
is one of the most well thought
out and detailed programs I have
seen on the Spectrum. The author
is a research chemist at Beecham
Pharmaceuticals so I'm sure we
can trust both the accuracy and
the relevance of this software!
MOLGRUM is just `12.50,including
postage from:
              DR. I. HUGHES,
              37 CHURCH WALK
              SAWBRIDGEWORTH
                  HERTS.
                 CM21 9BJ

 PLEASE STATE TAPE OR OPUS DISC

        "DISC ORGANISER"
   (for Disciple and +D Disc)
    Reviewed by C.Grant DIXON
   --------------------------


The purpose of this program is
to sort out the files on a given
disc, put them into sensible
order and generally tidy up what
may have been a very motley
collection of programs.

This may not appear to be a
large and useful program but
DISC ORGANISER offers so much
and is so well presented on the
screen that I have no hesitation
in recommending the program to
all Disciple/+D disc users.

The program arrives on cassette.
Instructions for transferring it
to disc are clear and simple but
first of all the program must be
customised by telling it what
drives you are using... i.e. 40
or 80 track; 1 or 2 sides;double
or single density. For a start
let us look at the MAIN MENU
which appears as a window over-
laying a CATalogue display of
the current drive. The commands
listed are:-

CATALOGUE      MAINTENANCE
LOAD PROGRAM   SECTOR CHECK
ORGANISER      SECTOR REPAIR
RENAME FILES   LPRINT CAT.
ERASE FILES    QUIT
COPY FILES     VIEW SCREEN
RECOVER FILES  ALTER DRIVE 1

Selection of a command is by
moving a highlighted area up and
down the list using the
appropriate arrow keys. ENTER
then executes the command. Some
of these are easily recognisable
but others require a word or two
of explanation.

1 .MAINTENANCE has a series of
commands allowing you to SAVE
ORGANISER; SAVE SYSTEM;CUSTOMISE
PROGRAM etc.

2.SECTOR CHECK goes through the
whole disc, checking each sector
in turn... it takes a long time!
If you have got a faulty sector
on side 2 you might have loaded
quite a few files before dis-
covering the fault. SECTOR CHECK

will give you confidence your
disc is O.K. before filling it
up. Note the process of checking
does NOT erase any recorded
data.

3.SECTOR REPAIR. Sometimes you
try to load a program and there
is a faulty sector ahead of it
which does not allow you to
reach the program. The REPAIR
facility appears to re-FORMAT
the faulty sector thereby losing
some data but in doing so allows
access to programs further into
the disc. Obviously this command
is only used as a last resort.

4.VIEW SCREEN removes the MENU
window and lets you read the
CATalogue which it overlaid.

5.ALTER DRIVE 1 toggles the
default value for the drive. The
new value is shown on the menu.

6.ORGANISER asks you to confirm
the customisation and gives you
the opportunity to re-customise.
It then asks you which program
is to be moved and what the
destination is. Files are always
referred to by number and not by
name and this gives a much
quicker entry. Gaps may be
created in the catalogue by
transferring files to high
numbers and then calling them
back into their new places
later. If you try to move a file
to a number which is already
occupied then no action is
taken.

When using some of the other
commands in the main menu such
as ERASE you are asked if you
want to do a single action or
"MULTIPLES". If you chose the
latter then you can chose
several files for action and
when "E" is pressed to indicate
the end of the selection all the
programs can be erased at one
go. It seems strange that this
could not have applied to the
ORGANISER command also..but this
is only a very minor criticism.

I was very impressed by the use
of a large number of window
display menus used to check the
various steps in the program.For
example, when you have made a
choice you may then be faced

with a menu stating your choice
and the words YES, NO, MAIN MENU
with the highlighting on the
word YES. You only have to press
ENTER to continue and this short
menu lets you have second
thoughts about your action.

The whole program is so easy to
use there is hardly any need for
an instruction manual and the
information sheet which comes
with the cassette is quite
adequate.
                       C.G.D.
Supplier..BETTERBYTES
          10 SPITTAL TERR.
          GOSFORTH
          NEWCASTLE-UPON-TYNE
          NE3 1UT

PRICE..`5 (cassette).
body_en:
### MOLGRUM by Dr. Ian Hughes
*reviewed by Brian Cavers*

MOLGRUM enables the construction and display of three-dimensional "stick and ball" representations of molecules which can be SAVEd, re-LOADed, edited, printed, zoomed, rotated, scrolled, and animated. Though written for a specialized field, MOLGRUM can portray not only molecules but other shapes in 3D and should interest anyone who likes wireframe graphics.

#### Features and Usage
Main control is by user-defined keys which move a BRIGHT panel over menu bars at the foot of the screen. There are 5 main menus accessed via UP/DOWN, with sub-menus for specific actions. While the manual is excellent and detailed, navigating between nested menus can be tricky for beginners.

I tested the software by constructing a cube. Inputting coordinates is flexible; you can enter values in sequence and correct/modify them by moving across a table. Once the wire-frame is built, you can twist, turn, zoom, and even create an animated "film show" of snapshots. You can also save the structure or individual screens as SCREEN$ files.

#### Printer Issues
As supplied, MOLGRUM is set up for the Epson LX80 printer. If you encounter strange characters (like a column of 'K's) on your interface, you can easily modify the printer codes in lines 58 and 66 of the BASIC loader. This "open" nature of the program is one of its greatest strengths.

#### Verdict
I cannot do it justice in the time I have available, but MOLGRUM is one of the most well-thought-out and detailed programs I have seen on the Spectrum. 

**Price:** £12.50
**Contact:** Dr. I. Hughes, 37 Church Walk, Sawbridgeworth, Herts, CM21 9BJ (Specify Tape or Opus Disc).

---

### DISC ORGANISER (for Disciple and +D Disc)
*reviewed by C. Grant Dixon*

The purpose of this program is to sort out files on a disc, put them into a sensible order, and generally tidy up a collection of programs. It is well-presented, easy to use, and highly recommended for all Disciple/+D users.

#### Main Features
- **Maintenance:** Customize program settings, save system files.
- **Sector Check:** Scans the whole disc for faulty sectors without erasing data.
- **Sector Repair:** Attempts to re-format faulty sectors to restore access to files.
- **Organiser:** Allows moving files by number for easier disc management.
- **Multiples:** Several operations (like ERASE) can be performed on multiple files at once.

The user interface relies on clear windowed menus that ask for confirmation before executing actions, preventing accidental data loss. Given the ease of use, the supplied information sheet is perfectly adequate.

**Price:** £5 (cassette)
**Supplier:** BETTERBYTES, 10 Spittal Terr., Gosforth, Newcastle-upon-Tyne, NE3 1UT.
body_ru:
### MOLGRUM, автор д-р Ян Хьюз
*обзор: Брайан Кейверс*

MOLGRUM позволяет создавать и отображать трехмерные «шаростержневые» модели молекул, которые можно сохранять (SAVE), загружать (re-LOAD), редактировать, печатать, масштабировать, вращать, прокручивать и анимировать. Хотя программа написана для узкоспециализированной области, MOLGRUM может отображать не только молекулы, но и другие фигуры в 3D — это будет интересно всем любителям каркасной графики.

#### Функции и использование
Основное управление осуществляется с помощью определяемых пользователем клавиш, которые перемещают яркую панель по пунктам меню в нижней части экрана. В программе 5 основных меню, доступных через клавиши UP/DOWN, с подменю для конкретных действий. Несмотря на то, что руководство пользователя отличное и подробное, навигация между вложенными меню может быть сложной для новичков.

Я протестировал программу, построив куб. Ввод координат реализован гибко: можно вводить значения последовательно и исправлять/изменять их, перемещаясь по таблице. Как только каркас построен, его можно вращать, масштабировать и даже создать анимированное «кино» из снимков экрана. Также можно сохранить структуру или отдельные кадры как файлы SCREEN$.

#### Проблемы с принтером
Изначально MOLGRUM настроена на принтер Epson LX80. Если вы столкнетесь со странными символами (например, колонкой букв «K») на вашем интерфейсе, вы можете легко изменить коды принтера в строках 58 и 66 базового загрузчика. Эта «открытость» программы — одна из её сильных сторон.

#### Вердикт
Я не могу полностью оценить её в рамках доступного времени, но MOLGRUM — одна из самых продуманных и подробных программ, что я видел на Spectrum.

**Цена:** £12.50
**Адрес:** Dr. I. Hughes, 37 Church Walk, Sawbridgeworth, Herts, CM21 9BJ (Укажите, что нужно: кассета или диск Opus).

---

### DISC ORGANISER (для дисков Disciple и +D)
*обзор: К. Грант Диксон*

Цель этой программы — упорядочить файлы на диске, привести их в логический порядок и навести порядок в коллекции программ. Это хорошо представленная, простая в использовании утилита, которую я без колебаний рекомендую всем пользователям Disciple/+D.

#### Основные функции
- **Maintenance:** настройка параметров программы, сохранение системных файлов.
- **Sector Check:** сканирование всего диска на наличие поврежденных секторов без удаления данных.
- **Sector Repair:** попытка переформатирования поврежденного сектора для восстановления доступа к файлам.
- **Organiser:** позволяет перемещать файлы по номерам для удобства управления диском.
- **Multiples:** операции (например, ERASE) могут выполняться сразу с несколькими файлами.

Интерфейс использует удобные окна меню, которые требуют подтверждения перед выполнением действий, предотвращая случайную потерю данных. Учитывая простоту использования, прилагаемого информационного листка более чем достаточно.

**Цена:** £5 (кассета)
**Поставщик:** BETTERBYTES, 10 Spittal Terr., Gosforth, Newcastle-upon-Tyne, NE3 1UT.
